components.text: Explain how simplicity can deny attribute composition while preserving distinct, meaningful predications of divine knowledge and power.
Explain how distinct divine attributes can be predicated without introducing the prohibited attribute composition.
Address whether knowledge and power must be distinct intrinsic properties in God.
Explain which distinctions remain permissible once positive intrinsic items distinct from God are excluded by the stated criterion.
Clarify how meaningful attribute and change predications can survive the denial of real intrinsic composition.
Clarify which distinctions are genuinely intrinsic positive items rather than conceptual or extrinsic predications.
Explain how attribute and contingent-predication distinctions avoid real intrinsic composition.
Show why divine independence must exclude every intrinsic distinction rather than only dependence on something external to God.
Challenge whether the proposed intrinsic boundary follows from aseity rather than being independently stipulated.
Address whether analogical predication by itself establishes the stronger metaphysical independence conclusion.
Show why aseity must exclude every intrinsic distinction rather than only dependence on something external.
Consider whether God as a whole could ground alleged parts or satisfy counterfactual dependence.
Answer the proposal that God as a whole could ground alleged intrinsic parts without compromising divine aseity.
Explain why distinct intrinsic items would generate a composite unity that is explanatorily prior to God.
Relate the general composition taxonomy to a specific grounding-based threat to divine unity.
Answer the proposal that God as a whole could ground alleged intrinsic parts.
Explain why composition threatens aseity even when the parts themselves do not ground God.
Explain how real Trinitarian persons and procession relations can be distinguished without becoming positive intrinsic constituents distinct from God.
Show how each person and relation can satisfy the identity requirement imposed on anything intrinsic to God.
Address the concern that Trinitarian multiplicity undermines the strong account of divine aseity.
Specify a Trinitarian model that avoids treating God as a composite community of persons.
Explain how real Trinitarian distinctions avoid positive intrinsic items distinct from God.
Identify a model preserving personal distinction without treating God as a composite community.
Explain how the Son can be begotten while God as such is not begotten if both are strictly identical in the proposed Latin model.
Show that the personal distinction is intrinsic rather than merely conceptual or creature-relative.
Apply the pro dependence rationale to an allegedly intrinsic personal distinction within God.
Test whether divine unity can remain noncomposite given asymmetric personal predicates.
Determine whether analogical predication resolves the asymmetric begotten and unbegotten predicates.
Explain how the Son can be identical with the Godhead when begottenness is asymmetrically true of the Son.
Show why the intrinsic Son does not satisfy the positive-item criterion for composition.
Explain why asymmetric begottenness does not entail a positive intrinsic ontological item distinct from the divine essence.
Answer the tetrad's claim that an eternal procession is a positive item intrinsic to but distinct from God.
Show why relational directedness fails the positivity-and-distinctness conditions in the stated part criterion.
Preserve divine aseity while recognizing a real relation between Father and Son.
Locate relational opposition without introducing an additional form of real intrinsic composition.
Explain why the Son's begottenness does not make him a positive intrinsic item distinct from God.
Reconcile the Son's relational begottenness with absolute identity with the divine essence.
Explain how knowledge attributions can vary with changing truths without God acquiring knowledge, losing knowledge, or realizing intrinsic potentiality.
Explain whether contingent knowledge can remain extrinsically differentiated when creaturely truthmakers or positive external items are absent.
Show why changing knowledge predicates do not identify a positive intrinsic item distinct from God.
Show that changes in true knowledge predications entail acquired knowledge or intrinsic change in God.
Establish that changing contingent truth introduces divine potentiality rather than merely extrinsic variation.
State what remains intrinsic to divine knowledge while explaining temporally different true knowledge attributions without intrinsic epistemic change.
Identify what divine contingent knowledge consists in apart from the positive extrinsic facts differentiating ordinary created worlds.
Explain why intrinsic intellect and causal efficacy do not introduce multiple positive items distinct from God.
Give a positive account of what divine knowledge consists in despite temporally different true attributions.
Identify an intrinsic basis for divine knowledge while locating contingent differentiation extrinsically.
Explain the difference between knowledge of past dinosaurs and their present extinction.
